Permitted Liens (§1.01) is a single defined term structured as a 51-clause enumerated list. The large majority of its clauses (e.g. (1),(4),(5),(7)-(17),(19),(22)-(45),(47)-(50)) are purely categorical/qualitative Lien carve-outs with no dollar, percentage, or ratio mechanic, and are intentionally not each modeled as a separate WireRule - doing so would not add computable economics and risks noise rather than fidelity.

The materially quantitative or ratio-gated sub-components were each modeled as an independent WireRule: the 30-day/good-faith-contest qualification shared by clauses (2)&(3) (r1) and the parallel test in clause (51) (r_51, an additional detected value not covered by the frozen inventory but structurally identical); the three-pronged ratio test in clause (20)(x)/(y)/(z) (r2, r3, r4); the General Lien Basket in clause (21) (r5); the classification/reclassification election in the closing paragraph (r6); and the cross-reference-heavy baskets in clauses (6), (18), and (46)(i)/(ii) (r7-r10), most of which are MISSING_CONTEXT or PARTIAL because their ultimate economics depend on Section 6.01/6.08 text that was out of scope for this submission.

All 6 frozen inventory items were consumed exactly once, each on the rule that carries its actual value/meaning (r1: 30-day test; r2: First Lien Leverage Ratio 2.00x; r3: Senior Secured Leverage Ratio/Interest Coverage Ratio alternative; r4: Total Leverage Ratio/Interest Coverage Ratio alternative; r5: $720.0mm/100% EBITDA General Lien Basket; r6: reclassification election).

The term 'Junior Lien Priority' gating clause (20)(y) has no detected definition anywhere in the instrument (confirmed via the supplied cross-reference resolution notes); this is preserved as an explicit dependsOn on r3 rather than guessed at.

'Available RP Capacity Amount' (clause (46)(i)) was successfully resolved via getDefinition and shown to be a shared ceiling with Section 6.08 (Restricted Payments) and the definition of 'Permitted Investments'; because those partner provisions are not part of this submission, the sharing relationship is preserved as explicit SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH dependsOn entries on r9 rather than a freestanding WireSharedCapacity with unresolvable members.

'Available Amount' (clause (46)(ii)) was searched for via getDefinition and does not exist under that name anywhere in the instrument package; r10 is marked MISSING_CONTEXT accordingly rather than guessed.

“ Available RP Capacity Amount ” means, at any time of determination (and after
giving effect to any reallocation or reclassification permitted hereunder), the amount of Restricted Payments that may be made at the time of determination pursuant to Section 6.08 or the definition of “Permitted Investments”;

clause (46)(i) of the definition of “Permitted Liens” (it being agreed and understood that, to the extent any Indebtedness has reduced the Available RP Capacity Amount pursuant to the foregoing proviso, the Available RP Capacity Amount
shall not be further reduced by the amount of any such Indebtedness that is secured by Liens pursuant to clause (46)(i) of the definition of “Permitted Liens”). The Initial Borrower may elect to allocate or reallocate from time to time
the Available RP Capacity Amount.

overallNotes: Permitted Liens (§1.01) is a single defined term structured as a 51-clause enumerated list. The large majority of its clauses (e.g. (1),(4),(5),(7)-(17),(19),(22)-(45),(47)-(50)) are purely categorical/qualitative Lien carve-outs with no dollar, percentage, or ratio mechanic, and are intentionally not each modeled as a separate WireRule - doing so would not add computable economics and risks noise rather than fidelity.

The materially quantitative or ratio-gated sub-components were each modeled as an independent WireRule: the 30-day/good-faith-contest qualification shared by clauses (2)&(3) (r1) and the parallel test in clause (51) (r_51, an additional detected value not covered by the frozen inventory but structurally identical); the three-pronged ratio test in clause (20)(x)/(y)/(z) (r2, r3, r4); the General Lien Basket in clause (21) (r5); the classification/reclassification election in the closing paragraph (r6); and the cross-reference-heavy baskets in clauses (6), (18), and (46)(i)/(ii) (r7-r10), most of which are MISSING_CONTEXT or PARTIAL because their ultimate economics depend on Section 6.01/6.08 text that was out of scope for this submission.

All 6 frozen inventory items were consumed exactly once, each on the rule that carries its actual value/meaning (r1: 30-day test; r2: First Lien Leverage Ratio 2.00x; r3: Senior Secured Leverage Ratio/Interest Coverage Ratio alternative; r4: Total Leverage Ratio/Interest Coverage Ratio alternative; r5: $720.0mm/100% EBITDA General Lien Basket; r6: reclassification election).

The term 'Junior Lien Priority' gating clause (20)(y) has no detected definition anywhere in the instrument (confirmed via the supplied cross-reference resolution notes); this is preserved as an explicit dependsOn on r3 rather than guessed at.

'Available RP Capacity Amount' (clause (46)(i)) was successfully resolved via getDefinition and shown to be a shared ceiling with Section 6.08 (Restricted Payments) and the definition of 'Permitted Investments'; because those partner provisions are not part of this submission, the sharing relationship is preserved as explicit SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH dependsOn entries on r9 rather than a freestanding WireSharedCapacity with unresolvable members.

'Available Amount' (clause (46)(ii)) was searched for via getDefinition and does not exist under that name anywhere in the instrument package; r10 is marked MISSING_CONTEXT accordingly rather than guessed.
